notes:
- Heavy focus: embeddings + reranking pipeline for customer-facing search.
- Key metrics: indexing scale ~200M vectors (long term), initial POC 10M vectors.
- Latency target: p95 <50ms query time overall (vector search + rerank), p99 <100ms.
- Cost target: avg cost per query <$0.005, aggressive.
- Preferred rerank approach: light-weight model for first-pass rerank (on dedicated GPUs) then expensive re-rank only for top-k.
- Connector requirements: bulk ingest, metadata-preserving upserts, similarity search with filtering by metadata/time, backpressure handling for large backfills.
- They host primary data in AWS us-east-1; want VPC peering or private link.
- Security: must support SSO (SAML), kms integration, audit logs export to SIEM, 7y retention policy for logs (legal).
- Quote from Head of Search: "We cannot risk noisy drift in embeddings — need model pinning and automated evals."
- Notes on vector stores: teams evaluated Pinecone (managed, easy), Weaviate (schema-flexible), pgvector (cost-effective, but connector maturity concerns), Elastic (already used for metadata index).
- Customer emphasized ability to route cold queries to cheaper model variants and fallback to hosted during peak.
- POC success criteria: ingest 10M docs within 48h, sustain 5k QPS with p95 <60ms, rerank latency added <30ms for top-5.
- Billing sensitivity: wants transparent token-level and per-query cost breakdown; open to committed capacity if latency/SLA guaranteed.
- Internal stakeholders: Head of Search (primary), Cloud Infra, Security/legal, Developer platform.
- "Short-term win": show Redwood->pgvector connector can do parallel bulk upserts with metadata and maintain sub-50ms vector nearest-neighbors on their hardware.
